reader.requirement: At --std 85 a COPY REPLACING pseudo-text-2 must be accepted with zero text words (empty, spaces only, or only a comment line: the match is deleted), one text word (including a lone separator comma, a text word in 1985), or many text words, and placed into the source as written.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.ReplacedTextIsLaidOutInFixedForm: the COBOL-85 layout rules of introduced lines

reader.edition-search: ScreenOperandPair puts no lower bound on pseudo-text-2 for a Whole replacement at any edition (only partial-word-2's upper bound, a 2002 form); read ApplyReplacements' edition parameter
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is a REPLACE statement (==XX4== BY ====); no COPY REPLACING pseudo-text-2 case of zero, comment-only or comma-only text

probes.expected: ==XDEL== BY ==== and ==YDEL== BY ==  == delete; many-word pseudo-text-2 makes W-C PIC X(4) VALUE "CCCC"; comment-only pseudo-text-2 deletes ZDEL; ==,== replaces QDEL
the shared operand parser accepts empty pseudo-text-2 (REPLACE witness)

citations.check: OK  §1985:XII.2.3 SR4  (2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: The one operand parser accepts every arity of pseudo-text-2 for whole replacement and ApplyReplacements inserts it as written; a probe with five pseudo-text-2 forms at --std 85 compiled and printed the derived values. A first variant whose replacement left ',.' glued was correctly refused (comma not followed by a space), which is the program's error, not this rule's.

refuter.evidence: Q13slash2-001 pseudo-text-2 only a '/' comment line: accepted, match deleted, [AAA]. Q14blank2-001 pseudo-text-2 only a blank line: accepted, [AAA]. Q15per2-001 ==XEND== BY ==.== (a lone separator period as pseudo-text-2): accepted, [FFF]. Q6debug2-001 pseudo-text-2 only a debugging line with WITH DEBUGGING MODE: accepted and placed, [DDD]. No lower bound on pseudo-text-2 at any edition in ScreenOperandPair. cite.py: OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR4.
